subject: Aurora Health security questionnaire: data decommissioning and retention assurances
messages:
From: Claire Zhao <c.zhao@aurorahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aurora Health Security <security@aurorahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API — decommissioning / final-delete evidence request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking our security questionnaire. A few follow-ups from our compliance team on data decommissioning for hosted tenants:

1) When a tenant terminates, what is the end-to-end timeline for destroying live data, cached tokens, and any snapshot backups? Please provide specific SLA windows (hours/days) and any manual steps.
2) How do you handle backups and cross-region replication — are there automated retention windows and proof of deletion?
3) Are there any scenarios where data is retained beyond the standard window (legal hold, backups in air-gapped archives)? If so, what is the process to request and verify a legal hold release?
4) Can you provide an example manifest or evidence artifact you produce after a completed tenant decommission?

We need this information for our vendor-risk attestation next week. If you can attach any playbooks or manifests that would help.

Regards,
Claire Zhao
Head of Security Operations
Aurora Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Zhao <c.zhao@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T13:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — decommissioning / final-delete evidence request

Claire — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attached are the playbook and a sample manifest. I'll follow up with a short timeline and the audit artifacts we can provide.

Summary (hosted API tenant decommissioning)
- Live data purge: initiated automatically on deprovisioning; primary deletion completed within 24 hours.
- Cache/KV eviction: KV caches and in-memory session stores are flushed immediately; residual cache references removed within 1 hour.
- Snapshot and backup lifecycle: automated lifecycle policies remove snapshots per tenant retention TTL (default 30 days) with final purge within 30-45 days depending on ongoing snapshots in-flight. Cross-region replicas follow the same lifecycle and are tombstoned concurrently.
- Evidence package: we provide a deletion manifest (CSV) listing object keys, deletion timestamps, and S3 lifecycle job IDs plus a signed statement. Sample attached: decommission_matrix.xlsx and backup_snapshot_manifest.csv.

Legal holds and exceptions
- Legal hold requests are only accepted from authorized Aurora signatories. When placed, the tenant's standard retention window is paused and a hold token is recorded with an audit entry. Release requests must be similarly authorized and produce a release audit chain.
- Holds are rare; for holds lasting >90 days we provide monthly attestation summaries.

Attachments included: retention_decommissioning_playbook.pdf (playbook), decommission_matrix.xlsx (sample manifest), backup_snapshot_manifest.csv (example).

I'll have Naomi add a short note about backup retention and any overwriting safeguards. If you want, we can also produce a signed DocuSign attestation after the decommissioning run.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Zhao <c.zhao@aurorahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — decommissioning / final-delete evidence request

Claire / Karthik — adding a couple of operational clarifications from the backups and storage team:

- Backup snapshots: we maintain incremental snapshots in S3 with tenant-scoped prefixes. Lifecycle rules apply an object tag (tenant-deleted:true) which triggers a multipart cleanup job. Cleanup jobs are batched nightly; for most customers final object deletion completes within 30 days of tenant deletion.
- Cross-region replication: replicas receive the same deletion marker; the replication controller acknowledges tombstones and schedules deletion in the remote region.
- Glacier/archived tiers: we do not proactively move tenant snapshots to cold storage after deprovision unless required by previously agreed addendum. If archived, deletions require an expedited restore-delete flow and are completed within 10 business days after authorization.
- Proof artifacts: our manifest includes object key, MD5, deletion-job-id, job-run-timestamp, and the operation user/service principal. We sign the manifest with an internal key and can provide a verification hash.

If Aurora needs a narrow SLA (e.g., 7-day final purge) we can propose a contractual add-on for dedicated retention and expedited snapshot purge.

-Naomi
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Claire Zhao <c.zhao@aurorahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aurora Health Security <security@aurorahealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T08:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — decommissioning / final-delete evidence request

Thanks — this is helpful. Two follow-ups:

1) Our procurement team requires a signed attestation after decommissioning (DocuSign OK). Can you confirm you can produce a signed statement that includes the manifest hash and deletion-job-IDs?
2) For the legal hold flow: please confirm the exact API/portal call and the list of required Aurora approvers (we'll provide those). We need the hold token ID and audit trail for our legal team.

If you can send a draft attestation we can run it through procurement. Also confirm whether any system-level logs (audit.log) containing deletion operations are retained longer than manifests and if so for how long.

Regards,
Claire
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Zhao <c.zhao@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — decommissioning / final-delete evidence request

Claire — confirmed. Next steps and scope we can commit to:

- Signed attestation: yes. We will generate a DocuSign-ready attestation that includes tenant-id, manifest SHA256, list of deletion-job-ids, and the timestamp of final object deletion. We will route that to your procurement signatory upon request. (example link to DocuSign prepared: https://app.docusign.com/aurora-decom-signature/ABC123)
- Legal hold API/portal: holds are created via the Redwood Console (Security > Holds) and via the Management API endpoint POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/holds. Required approvers: an Aurora security owner email and an Aurora legal owner email (we'll validate the signer list via an out-of-band CJIS-style verifier). The system returns a hold_token_id and an audit record.
- System logs: audit.log entries (user/service, operation, object key, job id, timestamp) are retained for 365 days by default for hosted customers. Manifests we produce are kept with a signed copy for 90 days and archived hashes for 365 days to support attestation verification.

We will: 1) prepare the DocuSign attestation draft and share the link by EOD tomorrow, 2) provide a one-page appendix showing a sample manifest hash verification process. If Aurora wants a shorter manifest retention or faster final purge SLA, we can convert that into a dedicated addendum.

Let me know whom to include on the DocuSign routing.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
